text: {"score":3,"justification":"The core numbers match the card (10.7% vs 2.8%, z 1.15, 36% low-complexity share, 29 charts, 3 documented 99215, 2 of 20 data-without-tests) and the language is cautious with an inconclusive leaning. But the headline and rationale contain a misleading framing and some unsupported or garbled content, and the examples and next steps are only partly useful.","problems":["Headline says '2 (6.9%) below the billed level', but both below-billed charts are 99214 claims; none of the 3 documented 99215 charts are below billed. Combined with 'Documentation largely supports billing', this blurs the point that the 99215 stratum is only 3 charts.","'Against 7% for the comparison providers' is the all-provider 99215 rate (0.067). This is a correct reading of the card but is not labeled clearly.","Note-check figures (problems 31%, data 3%) and '28% duplicate notes' are not on the evidence card. The 28% duplicate figure also conflicts with the 'late/unsigned 0%' framing and cannot be verified from the visible tool outputs, which cover other providers. '31% problem-count mismatch' is only a restatement of problems 31%.","The tool response listed deficiencies MISSING_SIGNATURE and MISSING_RESULTS, but the summary says 'unsigned 0%' and never mentions these deficiencies, which looks inconsistent and is not flagged.","Example claims mix two below-billed 99214 charts with two low-complexity 99215 claims. Neither the high-complexity 99215 claims nor the three documented, supported 99215 claims (C0035206, etc.) are shown, so the evidence is one-sided.","The next step names C0035228 and C0035556 as 99215 charts to request, but both are 99214 claims that are already documented. This is a mismatch and wastes the sample. It also gives no specific count for the targeted sample.","The summary does not note the by-complexity gradient (99215 share rises with condition count), which would help the investigator weigh upcoding against a sicker panel."]}
